semantic_rationale: GB020 asks for presence of definite/specific article; WALS 37A value includes only dedicated definite articles distinct from demonstratives. Near-exact: GB020=1 also covers 'demonstrative used as article' (a separate WALS 37A value), so GB020=1 is slightly broader.

wals_value_label: Demonstrative word used as definite article
semantic_rationale: Both mark a definite/specific article strategy. GB020=1 covers this case explicitly; WALS has it as a separate value.
Both WALS 37A 'No article' and GB020=0 assert absence of any definite/specific article. Near-exact; minor scope differences in what counts as an article.
GB021 asks whether indefinite/non-specific nominals commonly have indefinite articles. WALS 38A value is the same scope. GB021 explicitly cites WALS 38.
Both assert no indefinite article.
Presence of only definite article entails absence of indefinite article (GB021=0).

GB024=1 codes numeral before noun; WALS 89A 'Numeral precedes noun' is the same condition. Near-exact rather than exact because WALS 89A includes a 'numeral only modifies verb' value with no GB024 equivalent. GB024 cites WALS chapter 89.
GB024=2 codes numeral after noun; WALS 89A 'Noun precedes numeral' is the same condition. Same caveat as above.
GB024=3 codes 'both orders possible'; WALS 89A 'No dominant order' is closely related but defined via frequency/dominance rather than mere possibility. Directional match.

Both GB025=1 and WALS 88A code demonstrative-before-noun for adnominal demonstratives. Near-exact for free demonstratives; WALS 88A also includes separate affixal values with no GB025 equivalent. GB025 cites WALS chapter 88.
Same as above for the post-nominal value.
Demonstrative prefix is structurally prenominal but GB025 is designed for free-word demonstratives. Partial overlap.
Demonstrative suffix is structurally postnominal; same caveat.

GB065=1 codes possessor-before-possessed; WALS 86A 'Genitive precedes noun' is the same condition. Both focus on the pragmatically unmarked order. Minor caveat: WALS uses 'dominant' and GB uses 'pragmatically unmarked'.
Same as above for post-nominal possessor.
GB065=3 is 'both orders possible'; close but dominance vs possibility framing differs.
GB193=1 codes adnominal property word before noun; WALS 87A codes adjective before noun. Near-exact; WALS terminology is 'adjective' while GB uses 'adnominal property word'.
Same as above, post-nominal adjective/property word.
GB193=3 codes both orders; same caveat as other 'no dominant' mappings.

WALS 85A 'Prepositions' means prepositions are the dominant adposition type. GB074=1 means prepositions are present. WALS dominance implies GB presence, but not vice versa: a language may have prepositions (GB074=1) while its dominant adposition type is postpositions (WALS 85A=Postpositions). Directional: WALS 85A=Prep ⇒ GB074=1.
Same directional logic as for prepositions. WALS 85A=Postp ⇒ GB075=1.
WALS 85A 'No adpositions' means neither prepositions nor postpositions exist. GB074=0 & GB075=0 expresses the same condition directly. Near-exact.
If a language has both prepositions and postpositions with no dominant type, GB074=1 & GB075=1 is the closest formula. However, GB codes presence not co-dominance.
WALS 82A 'SV' codes subject-before-verb as dominant order in intransitive clauses. GB130=1 codes the same. Near-exact; minor dominance vs. pragmatic-unmarkedness framing difference.
WALS 82A 'VS' and GB130=2 both code verb-before-subject intransitive order.
WALS 83A 'OV' includes both SOV and OSV orders. GB133=1 codes verb-final transitive order. WALS OV ⇒ GB133=1, but GB133=1 also collapses OSV. Directional projection.

WALS 83A 'VO' includes SVO (GB132=1) and VSO/VOS (GB131=1). The formula is a disjunction not a conjunction; neither GB131=1 alone nor GB132=1 alone captures all VO languages. Partial: no single GB formula cleanly captures WALS VO.
WALS 81A SOV projects to verb-final (GB133=1). The compound formula further constrains verb-initial and verb-medial to 0, approximating SOV. OSV also projects to this formula — multi_value_collapse.
WALS 81A SVO projects to verb-medial (GB132=1). OVS also maps here — multi_value_collapse.
WALS 81A VSO projects to verb-initial. VOS also maps here.
VOS projects to verb-initial formula alongside VSO.
OSV is rare; projects to verb-final formula alongside SOV.
OVS projects to verb-medial alongside SVO.
